enrichment.introAneParallels: The world that produced this text was not empty of other stories. Neighboring cultures told their own accounts of how things began.
enrichment.introHistorical: What do we actually know about the world this text describes?
enrichment.introLinguistic: The Hebrew words themselves carry layers that translation inevitably compresses.
enrichment.introScientific: Modern science describes the natural world very differently from this ancient text. Neither validates nor invalidates the other — they answer different questions.

landing.hook: Every Bible translation adds words that aren't in the Hebrew. This one shows you which ones.
landing.conventionalVerse: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
landing.transparentVerse: In beginning, God created the skies and the land. And the land was chaos and void, and darkness *was* over the face of the deep, and wind/spirit of God *was* hovering over the face of the waters.
landing.diff1: Hebrew has no "the" before "beginning." We don't add it.
landing.diff2: The Hebrew word means physical sky — not a spiritual realm.
landing.diff3: The Hebrew word means both. We preserve the ambiguity.
landing.diff4: Every word we added for English grammar is in italics.
landing.howReading: Reading mode — continuous prose, clean page, just the text flowing. Read it like a story.
landing.howStudy: Study mode — verse by verse with color-coded notes. See the Hebrew, the ambiguity, the choices we made and why.
landing.who1: If you've read the Bible a hundred times and want to see what your translation smoothed over.
landing.who2: If you've never opened a Bible and want to know what it actually says before deciding what you think.
landing.who3: If you read Hebrew and want to check our work — everything is visible, nothing is hidden.
landing.scope: A translation of the Hebrew Bible from the Masoretic Text. In English, Portuguese, and German. Governed by 29 rules. It is not a devotional. It is not a replacement for scholarly editions. It is a disciplined attempt at transparency.
landing.scopeNot: It is honest about what it doesn't know.
landing.rulesPageSubtitle: The governance system behind the Transparent Translation.
landing.rulesIntro: Every translation makes choices. Most hide them. We wrote ours down.
landing.rulesPrimeDesc: If any rule conflicts with these four principles, the principles win.
landing.rulesPrime1: Do not simplify what the Hebrew keeps complex.
landing.rulesPrime2: Do not clarify what the Hebrew leaves ambiguous.
landing.rulesPrime3: Do not add what the Hebrew does not say — unless target grammar absolutely requires it.
landing.rulesPrime4: When addition is unavoidable, signal it clearly.
landing.rule1short: Same Hebrew word → same translation, by default. Every shift justified and logged.
landing.rule1example: אֶרֶץ (eretz) always → 'land.' Never randomly switching to 'earth,' 'world,' or 'region.'
landing.rule2short: If Hebrew supports two meanings and context doesn't force one, preserve both.
landing.rule2example: רוּחַ (ruach) → 'wind/spirit' — not resolved to one, because the Hebrew doesn't.
landing.rule3short: Don't sneak in later religious concepts not justified by the immediate Hebrew.
landing.rule3example: 'sky' not 'Heaven' — the Hebrew word means physical sky, not a spiritual realm.
landing.rule11short: Mark every word not in Hebrew. Distinguish what's translation from what's scaffolding.
landing.rule11example: 'And God saw that *it was* good' — italics show 'it was' is added for English grammar.
landing.rule25short: The Tetragrammaton rendered consonantally. Not 'the LORD.' Not silently substituted.
landing.rule25example: YHWH — because that is what the Hebrew consonants are. The vowels were never written.
